nodes.title: SG-10.2 Push the keyboard-focused object into the scene
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene already maps Tab and arrow keys to moveFocus and emits focusChange, and SceneObject.focus() already shows the hover highlight and label. The shared game store has no focus field, so React cannot push focus into the scene. Desired behavior: the store owns the focused object id, BootScene applies it to its SceneObjects, and shutdown removes focus. Expected result: a store focus change highlights the matching object with its label. Why: keyboard focus must look the same as hover.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a scene with objects, when the store focus id changes to an object id, then that SceneObject is focused and the others are blurred
- Given a focused object, when the scene shuts down, then every SceneObject is blurred and the store focus id is null
- Given the store focus id is null, when the store changes, then no SceneObject stays focused


## Scope
- In scope: game store focus field and setter
- In scope: BootScene focus sync from the store
- In scope: BootScene shutdown focus removal
- In scope: unit tests for all three
- Out of scope: React App or ActionMenu changes
- Out of scope: new events
- Out of scope: backend or API changes
- Out of scope: new visual styles for highlight
- Preserve: existing focusChange and menuClose emissions
- Preserve: SceneObject.focus and blur behavior
- Preserve: existing BootScene sync and shutdown cleanup


## Technical constraints
- Phaser 3.90 and zustand; no new dependencies
- Phaser is mocked in unit tests
- Reuse SceneObject.focus and blur


## Definition of done
- All requirements have Act and Verify units done
- Unit tests green


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Game store holds the focused object id
nodes.body:
Context: useGameStore in game/frontend/src/store/gameStore.ts holds only state, setState and init. Desired behavior: add a focusedObjectId field (default null) and a setFocusedObject action. Expected result: any module can set and read the focused object id. Why: the scene needs a shared place to read focus from.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a fresh store, when focusedObjectId is read, then it is null
- Given the store, when setFocusedObject('bookshelf') is called, then focusedObjectId is 'bookshelf'
- Given a focused id, when setFocusedObject(null) is called, then focusedObjectId is null


## Scope
- In scope: gameStore focus field and action
- Out of scope: scene changes
- Preserve: init and setState semantics


## Technical constraints
- Keep init and setState behavior unchanged


## Definition of done
- Field and action exist with typed signatures


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · BootScene shows store focus with the hover highlight and label
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene subscribes to useGameStore and calls onStateChange; Tab and arrows call moveFocus and emit focusChange. Desired behavior: onStateChange focuses the SceneObject whose spec.id equals focusedObjectId and blurs the rest, and the keyboard handler stores the focused id. Expected result: a store focus change shows the same highlight and label as hover. Why: one source of truth for focus.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given objects bookshelf and bed, when focusedObjectId becomes 'bed', then bed.focus() is called and bookshelf.blur() is called if it was focused
- Given focusedObjectId is null, when the store changes, then a focused object is blurred
- Given Tab is pressed, when focus moves, then focusedObjectId in the store equals the focused object id and focusChange is still emitted


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene.onStateChange focus application
- In scope: BootScene.onKeyDown store write
- Out of scope: shutdown cleanup
- Preserve: focusChange emission
- Preserve: sync(state) for each object


## Technical constraints
- Reuse SceneObject.focus and blur; do not render highlight in BootScene


## Dependencies
- REQ-1


## Definition of done
- Store focus drives scene highlight
- Keyboard path writes the store


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Focus is removed when the scene shuts down
nodes.body:
Context: the SHUTDOWN handler in BootScene.create unsubscribes the store, destroys effects, objects and sprites. Desired behavior: before destroying objects it blurs each one and sets focusedObjectId to null. Expected result: no stale focus survives a scene restart. Why: a remounted scene must not start with a phantom highlight.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a focused object, when SHUTDOWN fires, then blur() is called on every SceneObject
- Given focusedObjectId is 'bed', when SHUTDOWN fires, then the store focusedObjectId is null
- Given SHUTDOWN has fired, when the store focus changes afterwards, then no SceneObject focus or blur call occurs


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene SHUTDOWN handler
- Out of scope: React unmount
- Preserve: existing destroy and unsubscribe cleanup


## Technical constraints
- Unsubscribe from the store before writing null so the scene is not re-entered


## Dependencies
- REQ-1


## Definition of done
- Shutdown removes scene and store focus


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: At the top of onStateChange, before the null-state return, read focusedObjectId from useGameStore.getState() and loop this.sceneObjects: if o.spec.id === focusedObjectId call o.focus(), else if o.isFocused call o.blur().
steps.expected: Changing the store focus id focuses exactly the matching object.

steps.action: In the delta !== 0 branch, after moveFocus, compute const focusedId = this.sceneObjects.find((o) => o.isFocused)?.spec.id ?? null; call useGameStore.getState().setFocusedObject(focusedId) and reuse focusedId in the existing focusChange emit.
steps.expected: Tab stores the focused id and still emits focusChange.
